hook: Matei Zaharia grew up partly in Toronto and earned an undergraduate degree from the University of Waterloo before pursuing a PhD in computer science at UC Berkeley's AMPLab. There, starting in 2009, he created Apache Spark, an in-memory cluster computing engine that grew into one of the most widely used frameworks for large-scale data processing, and co-created the cluster manager Apache Mesos. After completing his PhD in 2013, he co-founded Databricks with Ion Stoica and other Berkeley colleagues to commercialize Spark, taking on the role of Chief Technology Officer. He held a faculty position at MIT CSAIL before moving to Stanford University, where he is now an associate professor of computer science co-directing research on data and AI systems. At Databricks he has also helped build MLflow and Delta Lake, and his more recent research examines combining large language models with external data sources.

timeline.event: Co-authors "Resilient Distributed Datasets: A Fault-Tolerant Abstraction for In-Memory Cluster Computing" at NSDI
timeline.impact: Formalizes the RDD abstraction underpinning Apache Spark's fault tolerance model

timeline.event: Completes his PhD at UC Berkeley and co-founds Databricks with Ion Stoica and other AMPLab colleagues
timeline.impact: Launches a company to commercialize Apache Spark, later becoming its CTO

timeline.event: Receives the ACM Doctoral Dissertation Award
timeline.impact: His PhD dissertation on Spark is recognized as an outstanding contribution to computer science

timeline.event: Joins Stanford University as an assistant professor of computer science after a faculty position at MIT CSAIL
timeline.impact: Continues academic research on data systems alongside his role at Databricks

timeline.event: Receives the Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers
timeline.impact: Recognized by the U.S. government for early-career contributions to computer science research

timeline.event: Receives the ACM Prize in Computing
timeline.impact: Honored for his contributions to large-scale data systems including Apache Spark

quick_facts: Created Apache Spark as a PhD student at UC Berkeley's AMPLab starting in 2009
Co-founded Databricks in 2013 and serves as its Chief Technology Officer
Associate Professor of Computer Science at Stanford University, previously an assistant professor at MIT CSAIL
Co-created Apache Mesos, MLflow and Delta Lake
Recipient of the 2025 ACM Prize in Computing and the 2019 Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers

achievements.title: Co-founder and CTO of Databricks
achievements.impact: Helped grow Databricks into one of the largest privately held data and AI infrastructure companies.

achievements.title: Co-creator of MLflow and Delta Lake
